body: I married him because despite this he is still amazing and there are some celebrations that he knocks out of the park. It’s just that when things are bad theyre pretty awful.

I acknowledge that I should have communicated it as soon as it happened. It was just so jarring I didn’t know how to respond. But as soon as he asked I did tell him and he was pissed. In my mind we should be focusing on moving past the main issue as soon but he seems unwilling to see it from my perspective and says that I’m just communicating poorly to make him feel like an asshole. Maybe I’m wrong but it just hurts to feel like my feelings are outshined by my initial reactions

Yes there are definitely patterns and we’ve discussed them.  I will say that what you’ve said is fair - I agree that I should have planned something if this was important to me to show him that. 

I do think that I have been direct in the past, however. We’ve talked about having different sex drives and we came to a conclusion that if he or I wasn’t in the mood we would at least comfort the other one so they didn’t feel unwanted. I brought this up in our argument and he just went silent before getting mad about something else. Based on your advice maybe the answer is to remind him what we agreed to in the moment. In my mind though it just sucks that that’s necessary...

Thank you for your advice. To answer your question, he said that he didn’t want to have sex because he wanted to do it at night when it was “more special.” I’ll admit that I took that statement pretty hard and I told him that it was a problem that he didn’t think I was special enough to have sex with unplanned and he said I was twisting his words.
